title: Enhancing Collaborative Design in Concurrent Engineering: A Conceptual Synthesis and Research Framework for Team-Based Product Development
content: Concurrent engineering (CE) is a process that integrates product, process, manufacturing, service and life cycle design decisions into concurrent activities instead of sequential activities. Not only is its potential related to team composition of experts, but also to how teams share knowledge, deal with dependencies, communicate design intent and address trade-offs in a time-critical environment. This manuscript builds upon the idea that a conscious application of group design can enhance innovation and accelerate development time and first-time-right product performance, but that group design can also lead to coordination overhead, group-think, conflict, and more iterations. It builds an integrative conceptual framework that connects collaborative design practices to design process results via knowledge integration, shared situational awareness, decision quality and capability for change management. The framework categorizes the following: structural conditions (team composition, task interdependence and governance); process mechanisms (communication, shared digital representations, constructive conflict and design reviews); enabling infrastructure (CAD, product data management, product life cycle management, simulation and digital-thread capabilities); and outcomes (novelty, quality, rework, lead time and life cycle value). There are three research questions and testable hypotheses that are stated. A future systematic or scoping review is proposed, with a transparent, reproducible review protocol, and a mixed-method empirical approach to testing the review protocol without suggesting that data have already been gathered. The paper presents a multilevel model, operational definitions, measurement ideas, boundary conditions and a research agenda for collaborative design in modern CE, such as distributed teams, AI-supported design and Industry 5.0 centered CE. As no original experiment, survey or interview data set is provided for this manuscript, the article instead offers a conceptual synthesis and proposed research protocol instead of fabricated empirical findings.
